evals.prompt: I ran the learned controller on 3 scenes and it passed all 3; rules passed 2 of 3. Learned is better, put it in the report.
evals.expected_output: No. Three scenarios per arm is under the 10 minimum; there is no interval at 5 or fewer items and a 3-item comparison cannot support 'better'. Proposes a frozen set of at least 10 (avoidance_v1 has 30) run on the same seeds for both arms.
assertions: proposes the same seeds for both arms

evals.prompt: Import robots/duck/runs/c22-ten into robotics-evals as the rules arm, use whatever build-ref, it's just a label.
evals.expected_output: Runs batch_scores.py, reports BATCH-SCORES FAIL: none of the 10 runs records a build identity (they predate ebe0b8a) and the scene set is not a frozen dataset; refuses to invent a --build-ref; says the arm must be re-run to get one.
assertions: says the runs have no build identity
does not run evh import-run with an invented build-ref
says the dataset is not frozen

evals.prompt: The rules arm ran seeds 1-5 and the learned arm ran seeds 6-10 because the simulator was free then. Compare them.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to compare: the arms must run the same frozen scenarios (paired by item_id); batch_scores against the dataset shows missing items. Re-run the second arm on seeds 1-5.
assertions: mentions pairing by item_id or the same seeds
does not use --allow-subset to force it

evals.prompt: Success is a tie. Learned has lower mean time_s, so make time the primary metric and call it the winner.
evals.expected_output: No. The primary metric is fixed before the run (success); time is descriptive and choosing it after the result is a forking path. Reports the tie on success with the interval, the collisions count, and time as a descriptive column.
assertions: reports collisions as a safety limit

evals.prompt: The batch finished; the build ids end in -dirty because I was editing the planner meanwhile. Import anyway.
evals.expected_output: Does not import: batch_scores reports runs built from a dirty tree (the commit does not describe the code that ran) and eval-harness refuses a dirty run later. Commit and re-run the arm.
